key_insight: UNSM-treated Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings showed sample-dependent hardness, with peak values at 20 N/20 µm for detonation-sprayed coatings and 30 N/30 µm for HVOF coatings.
engineering_relevance: Coating route and UNSM settings should be evaluated together with surface integrity rather than selecting treatment conditions by hardness alone.
method: Evaluated four UNSM-treated samples per deposition route at static loads of 20 or 30 N and vibration amplitudes of 20 or 30 µm.
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN with a 10 s dwell.
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and 546–1165 HV for HVOF coatings; post-scratch SEM showed heterogeneous contrast and crack-like discontinuities in both series.
watch_item: Post-scratch SEM observations do not isolate UNSM-induced damage or establish a scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
